Intermediate: Work on expanding vocabulary, improving grammar, and developing confidence in holding longer conversations and expressing ideas.

Intermediate: Dive into complex grammar topics like conditionals, reported speech, and advanced sentence patterns to elevate your writing and speaking.

teacher_info.introduction:
The method that I like to focus most on with students is this: First of all, I try to become familiar with your interests, your profession etc. Then I try and find an article or documentary based on a topic that we have agreed to talk about. We both need to work together to think of the best topics to discuss. We can talk about technology, business, history, cultural topics etc. Anything that is genuinely interesting. No boring material! I'll send you the material a few days before the class, so that you have some time to study the article or documentary, so that you build new vocabulary and become familiar with the topic. You have now gained "passive vocabulary" which should be fresh in your mind. Then in the lesson, my job is to get you talking about the topic as much as possible for an hour while keeping the conversation flowing (I try to be a little quieter and let you do most of the talking), and I also focus on providing strong correction on pronunciation, grammar, natural language etc. And every lesson we can cover a new topic so that you can build on new areas of your vocabulary. This is all about "activating" vocabulary and developing your speaking fluency.

Another method that I use is "grammar stories/logic". Basically, grammar books are sometimes highly confusing and frustrating, so what I do is try to get students to become more fluent in the grammar patterns and what they represent imaginatively/mentally. What do you imagine in your mind when you hear the sentences "Yesterday, I read a book" and "Yesterday, I was reading a book"? These two grammar structures should represent different "picture/movie logics" within your mind when you hear them. Unfortunately, the grammar "logic" in your first language interferes with English logic, so my job is to explain this English grammar "logic" as best I can. It's a very interesting method which I'm pretty sure hasn't been used before.

I also like to study pronunciation at a detailed level with students.

*These can be done in a more fun/relaxed style or a more serious/strict presentation style, depending on your goals*

This increases your speaking time in each class. If you want I can be more conversational, we can even debate topics a little, but this will limit your speaking time. pro_course_detail.title: 'Question/Answer' Grammar Fluency Training
pro_course_detail.description: Most students have studied grammar in schools using very academic methods, by just studying grammar rules & explanations, without too much real world practice. In my 'grammar fluency training' classes it's all about USING natural grammar as much as possible. In the class we'll watch an interesting video together, and then based on the story in the video, I'll ask you a question with a specific grammar tense ("What are some things you think he'll be doing this morning?"), and then you need to answer using the same grammar tense, the future continuous ("I think he'll be getting ready, he'll also be eating some breakfast, and then he'll be travelling to work"). If you have problems answering we can quickly look at the logic of the grammar. When you answer using the same grammar tense as my question, this means that for most of the class I can push you to use all the available grammar tenses (past, present, future, conditional, passive etc) as much as possible. You can even practice asking me the questions using all those grammar tenses (question grammar can get difficult). The goal here is for you to USE all the different grammar tenses in natural conversation, repeating the grammar patterns again and again and again talking about different topics. All of the grammar tenses need to be used hundreds of times to eventually become automatic. Students really enjoy this grammar method as they have the chance to understand and use grammar connected to situations & stories. It's easier to understand the logic of grammar when it's connected to a real life situation (which we'll see in the video)

pro_course_detail.title: IELTS Speaking Preparation
pro_course_detail.description:
To help prepare you for the speaking part of the IELTS test, we can start out by just practicing your answers to common questions in a relaxed way to get you comfortable with the questions while I offer suggestions on high scoring vocabulary, grammar etc. We can focus on all the different things that you need to remember during the speaking test like using linking words (additionally, first of all, in conclusion, lastly etc). 

After the 'relaxed preparation' stage we can start simulating the test to get you familiar with the serious style and timing of the test. I'll use a stop watch to keep track of times and we can prepare in a more realistic setting & style. I'll still offer corrections and suggestions. We can record this as well if you wish.

The goal of all of this is to get you using more linking words, using high scoring vocabulary and grammar (e.g passive grammar gets you easy extra points), speaking with enthusiasm without pauses, and just to present your answers in a confident way to give the examiner a good impressions of your speaking skills.

pro_course_detail.title: Business English (Job Interviews, Presentations, Meetings, Career Topic Discussions etc)
pro_course_detail.description:
JOB INTERVIEW PREPARATION:
If you have a job interview coming up, we can practice the common questions that come up (strengths & weaknesses etc) while I focus on giving corrections/suggestions etc to get you comfortable answering those questions (mostly soft skills questions). We can also find technical questions for your area (hard skills questions) and you can be as technical as you want with your answers while I focus on corrections. 

MEETINGS:
To help you prepare a little better for business meetings, we can study & discuss articles and videos about the topic. I like to use 'Harvard Business Review' as they have a lot of great articles about meeting structures, chairing meetings effectively etc, and there are also a lot of great role play videos which we can study and discuss. 

PRESENTATIONS:
If you have any work presentations coming up, you can prepare for your presentation before the class, and maybe send me the PowerPoint file on Skype so that I can become familiar with your topic before class, and then when you come to class you can basically practice giving your presentation for one hour while I focus on giving corrections/suggestions etc. You can share your desktop screen so I can see the presentation as well while you talk about it.

DISCUSSIONS ABOUT WORK TOPICS:
If there is anything at work that you need to be fluent in when speaking, you can basically tell me all about the topic while I focus on corrections. I might not an expert about the exact topic but I can still focus on correcting pronunciation, grammar etc (I've taught students from nearly most professions though so I can follow pretty well). Just start out speaking about the big picture and then zoom into all the tiny technical details of the topic. For example, one of my IT students shares her desktop screen with me to explain the coding and programming work that she does.
